summary:
Navigator is a multiplayer augmented-reality game where players design a real space mission under the same engineering constraints NASA faces. They select a destination (7 planets), choose an engine, propellant, power source, antenna, launch vehicle, and science instruments — all within a budget and a mass limit. The Tsiolkovsky rocket equation links every choice in real time.

Players then pick their launch date from a real porkchop plot generated from NASA/JPL Keplerian elements and a Lambert solver: launch outside the window and it costs thousands of m/s. They fly the mission with real Newtonian gravity and gravity assists, survive mid-cruise anomalies, and operate their science instruments at the planet before the communication pass ends.

The final debrief explains every decision, recomputes "what if you had chosen differently?" with the real equations, and compares the player's spacecraft with the actual NASA mission that flew the same profile (Mariner, Juno, Perseverance, Cassini, Voyager).

Play now in any browser — no install: https://space.guacalita.co
details:
Navigator puts the player in the role of a NASA mission designer. Every design choice has a real consequence driven by real physics.

DESIGN

7 destinations (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) × 3 objectives (flyby, orbit, landing). The player configures engine (chemical/ion/nuclear), propellant, power (solar/RTG/reactor), antenna, launch vehicle, and 8 science instruments — all within a budget and mass limit enforced by the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation in real time.

LAUNCH WINDOW

A porkchop strip shows ΔV cost for every launch date in the synodic cycle, calculated from NASA/JPL Keplerian elements + universal-variable Lambert solver + patched conics. Validated against real windows: Mars Nov 2026 & Dec 2028, Venus Jul 2026 & Mar 2028.

FLIGHT & SCIENCE

AR flight with real Newtonian gravity and assist rings (free ΔV, like Voyager 2). Mid-cruise anomalies (solar storm, failure, blackout) must be resolved with available resources. Science only scores if the antenna downlinks the data before the pass ends, with the real light-travel delay per planet.

LANDING

7 unique surface missions: sky crane on Mars, Venera lander on Venus, Dragonfly drone on Titan, atmospheric probes on Jupiter and Uranus, rocket descent on Mercury and Triton.

DEBRIEF

Cause → effect for every subsystem. "What if?" lines recomputed with real equations. Comparison card: player design vs. the real NASA mission.

MULTIPLAYER

P2P via QR code — no server, no accounts. 2–4 players share 4 mission roles. One team result.

OTHER MODES

Campaign (8 missions, world map, star ratings), free-flight Solar System, teacher mode for classrooms, sky finder powered by NASA JPL Horizons (point your phone at the sky — see where your planet is tonight).

TOOLS & LANGUAGES

Unity 6 (C#, URP), Flutter (host app), Iroh/Senda (P2P networking), Python (orbital mechanics validation), Meshy AI (3D models), Claude Code (coding assistant).

Live demo (browser, no install): https://space.guacalita.co

Source code: https://github.com/jolugoba/navigator-spaceapps
